1. Heard Ms. Tamanna Parveen, Advocate holding brief of Shri K.K.Tewari, learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2. No one appears on behalf of the respondent no.2 despite service of notice.
3. In terms of the F.I.R., initially a missing person report was lodged.

Subsequently, in the statements under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the victim did not support the prosecution story and stated that she knew the applicant and she has gone alongwith the applicant to Lucknow where she stayed around four days.
The victim also admitted of forming physical relations with the applicant.
In the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., a similar statement was made, however it was stated that the applicant has hypnotized her and committed rape upon her.

sentences.text: As per the Adhaar Card, age of the victim is around 18 years whereas as per the primary school certificate, relied upon by he learned A.G.A., the age of the victim is about 14 years.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant further argued that as there is no document on record prescribed under the Juvenile Justice Act and the rules framed thereunder to form a view with regard to age determination of the victim, as such the same would be decided at the time of trial in view of the law laid down in the case of Monish Vs. State of U.P. passed by this Court in Crl. Misc.
Bail Application No.55026 of 2021 decided on 9.2.2023.

entities.text:

Bail Application No.55026 of 2021
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: The applicant has no criminal history and is in jail since 6.7.2023, hence the applicant may be enlarged on bail.

6. Considering the fact that the two statements of the victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. do not corroborate the prosecution story; the applicant has no criminal history and is languishing in jail since 6.7.2023; the age of the victim is to be determined at the time of the trial in view of the law laid down in the case of Monish Vs. State of U.P.(supra) as well as in terms of the Juvenile Justice Act and the rules framed thereunder, and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and
without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
7. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

8. Let the applicant Neeraj Kumar be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.261 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366, 376 I.P.C. and Section 5L/6 of the POCSO Act, Police Station Ramsanehi Ghat,
District Barabanki on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions :-
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
